Live pass admitted iff 64 x history-octets <= pool: development preset (A 32,768) pool 3,441,664 so h <= 53,776 octets; default A (16 MiB) pool 64 MiB so h <= 1 MiB. No profile setting funds it (H is not in the pool; red2 with 64 MiB H refused the same 452,968,896). The proposed fix (a measured live copy count) cannot close it: one 16x list copy of the S152 history is 113 MB and the post-flip non-arena state of 2,100 records (48n + 2n x 4,160 + 8 used) about 74 MB, both far past 3.4 MB. Where the pass's second state comes from is the decision: (A) a reclaim term in the figure (every node's dynamic space grows), (B) the pass holds room in the store budget while it runs (POST admission changes during a pass), or (C) the open's completion reserve (about 1.2 GB at development bounds, idle after the open, never admitted against by the ledger's own comment; needs a repay transition in memory-credits). scenario: A node with the default developer profile accumulates a few thousand articles with an expiry policy. Every live store reclaim answers deferred-credit, the expired payloads are never released, and the disk keeps growing although the policy says they expire. Only an operator-raised history bound (a larger reservation) lets the pass run.
